demo_desc.title: Solving Two-Step Equations
demo_desc.body:
This mathematics visualization/simulation helps students learn and solve basic two step equations with one variable. Students will have to experiment with the features of the demo, interact with the objects (apples and candies), and investigate what rules make the scale equal.

Our demonstration promotes visual and hands-on learning, as opposed to instruction guided memorization techniques. We will guide students in the right direction, but students playing with the demo for 5-10 minutes should receive a basic sense of how to solve basic equations (2x+12=5x+3). The many visualization techniques in the demo should help kids visualize the objects on the scale, inspiring creativity and deep thinking.

Students can also try very simple, automatically generated practice problems in a visual manner.

about.text1: Conception is a non-profit fundraiser created by a group of freshmen at Needham High School with one thing in common: A love of math.
about.text2:
We want to share our love of learning to younger audiences by teaching more complex mathematical ideas to younger elementary students in creative and visual ways.
For instance, we will teach students how to solve two-step equations with visual demos. That way, it is easy to understand AND fun to learn! By associating math with fun experiences, we can help educate and bring back interest in math at a time of decreasing interest (see home page for more info).


WHY?
  • On a serious note: when I was in elementary school, the options for learning math for free were few and far in between. I believed, and still do, that the math curriculum at school was inadequate and not designed to give students interest or additional opportunities to challenge themselves. The only ways I could challenge myself in math was to watch online videos and teach myself online (see cool websites). There were no free math lessons anywhere. My parents tried their best to tutor me, but they also had to learn by searching online. At the first opportunity I had, I started this organization to help inspire, motivate, and educate underrepresented students that want to pursue math in their career, but lack resources or privileges to do so. I vow to fill the lack of a helpful AND free mathematics program by creating one myself for others like me.

  • Impacts of free education programs: Free mentorship or classes has had many impacts on my education. I learned debate through a virtual debate class through the BrightMoon Foundation. That experience with debate, synthesizing arguments, and public speaking has stayed with me for 6 years. More importantly, I genuinely had a lot of fun attending the debate class. The class played a large part in my decision of joining the High School Speech and Debate team. Furthermore, I also learned how to play the violin exclusively through a free High School tutoring program called Notelove. If not for my tutor, I would not have been nearly as good at the violin without them. I understand the impact of programs like these myself, hence why I want to return the favor with Conception. Conception: Education lies the power to change lives, even if it's just a concept.
